notes:
Summary: Avalon is a large fintech provider evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for latency-sensitive inference. Primary focus: autoscaling and capacity management (scale-up/scale-down policies, warm pools, queueing/backpressure) to meet strict p99 SLOs while controlling cost.

Key technical requirements / asks (paraphrased):
- Throughput targets: steady-state 1,200 TPS (embeddings batch mode), burst up to 4k TPS for short windows (3-10s).
- Latency SLOs: chat p95 < 150ms, reranking p99 < 400ms, embeddings p95 < 200ms.
- Capacity planning: reserved GPUs for baseline load; ability to autoscale with predictable warm-up time and explicit warm pool sizing. Interested in on-prem options for data residency.
- Warm pools: want pre-warmed kernels and KV-cache priming for model variants. Asking for guidance: warm pool as % of baseline vs absolute GPU counts.
- Scale policies: need scale-up aggressive (fast spin-up) and scale-down conservative (longer cooldown) to avoid thrashing. Suggested thresholds: scale-up at queue length > 8 per worker or CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 10s; scale-down after 5m of utilization < 30%.
- Queueing/backpressure: prefer head-of-line priority for interactive traffic, background batch embeddings to be queued with backpressure + SLA-aware re-routing to secondary region. Want Redwood's queue behavior documented (max queue depth, overflow behavior, circuit-breaker/backoff strategy).
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller-quantized model variants for cold starts; must maintain deterministic latency bounds.
- Reserved GPU ask: planning 10 x H100-equivalent reserved nodes for baseline, with burst pool of 6 additional GPUs to be billed as reserved or burst capacity? Finance team needs pricing tradeoffs (monthly reserved vs burst credits).

Recent Quotes / Call snippets:
- "If warm pools cost as much as idle reserved GPUs we won't be able to justify continuous pre-warming" — Avalon ML Lead
- "We need a deterministic p99 for regulatory SLAs, even during region failover" — Head of Platform

POC plan & success criteria:
- Run 2-week POC on Dedicated: week 1 functional + integration; week 2 stress tests.
- Test scenarios: steady baseline, 10x sudden burst, gradual ramp, region failover.
- Acceptance: meet p95/p99 targets across scenarios with defined cost per 1M tokens under budget threshold.

- Data residency: planning for private control plane in NA; require audit log retention 7 years (ask from compliance).
